CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF COLLECTION: [redacted date]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing at 14 weeks gestation by ultrasound. Maternal age 39 years. Suspected chromosomal abnormalities including Down syndrome (trisomy 21).

SPECIMEN TYPE
Amniotic fluid

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded chromosome analysis post-amniocentesis

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XX

Normal female karyotype. No trisomy 21 or other numerical/structural abnormalities detected.

INTERPRETATION
G-banded analysis of cultured amniocytes reveals a normal female chromosome complement. No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other chromosomal abnormalities was detected within the resolution limits of this analysis (approximately 5-10 Mb). This result supersedes previous rapid PCR analysis.

LIMITATIONS
This test cannot detect balanced rearrangements that do not result in gain or loss of chromosomal material, low-level mosaicism (<20%), or submicroscopic deletions/duplications below the resolution of conventional cytogenetics.

RECOMMENDATION
Normal female karyotype indicates absence of chromosomal abnormalities within test resolution limits. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and any additional testing considerations.

This laboratory is accredited by CAP (#[redacted ID]) and CLIA certified (#[redacted ID]).

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director

Verified by:
[redacted name], CLSp(CG)
Cytogenetics Technologist
